full_judgment:
Md Ali Asgar Khan J: This appeal under section 30(1) of the Special Powers Act, (Act XIV of 1974) arises out of the order dated 3-2-99 passed by the learned Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal No.1 Rangpur in Special Tribunal Case No. 30 of 1998 pending in the Court for trial rejecting an application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for discharging the accused appellants namely 1 Shaheb Ali 2 Abdul Hoque and 3 Md Kabir against whom the police submitted final report. 

 2. The allegations against the accused-appellants and 2 others are that, six bottles of Phensidyl were recovered from the possession of Md Selim alias Montu and Nawshad Ali who on interrogation told the police that the accused appellants are also involved with them in connection with the smuggling of six bottles of Phensidyl. On this allegation the First Information Report was lodged. Police after investigation submitted charge-sheet against two accused persons namely, 1 Selim and 2 Nawshad and First Information Report against the accused appellants. The learned Special Tribunal on receipt of the charge-sheet framed charge against the accused persons namely, Selim and Nawshad and also against the accused-appellants under section 25B of the Special Powers Act against whom the Investigating Officer after investigation submitted FRT. It is against this order of framing charge the accused-appellants have preferred this appeal in which further proceedings of Special Tribunal Case No.30/1998 has been stayed. 

 4. We have perused the First Information Report, the charge-sheet including the impugned order of the learned Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal. The police as it appears submitted FRT against the accused-appellants as one of the witnesses implicated them in this case in which six bottles of Phensidyl were recovered from the possession of the co-accused Md Selim alias Montu and Nawshad Ali. The learned Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal framed charge against the accused appellants holding that the statements under section 161 CrPC cannot be looked into at the time of framing charge under section 241 A of the CrPC which is a misconceived one. Police after holding investigation and examining of witnesses under section 161 of the CrPC submitted FRT against the accused appellants as none of the witnesses implicated the accused-appellants in this case as to recovery of six bottles of Phensidyl. 

 5. The learned Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal disregarding the statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the CrPC framed charge against the accused appellants which is a misconceived one in view of the decision in the case of HM Ershad vs Stare reported in 45 DLR 533 wherein it has been held that consideration of the statements made under section 161 of the CrPC while framing of charge or otherwise is a necessary part of the Court's duty. 

 7. In this view of the facts and the. circumstances of the case and our discussions as above, we find that the learned Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal acted illegally in framing charge against the accused appellants under section 25B of the Special Powers Act as there is absolutely no evidence against them and the continuation of the proceedings should be an abuse of the process of the court and law for which this appeal should be allowed after setting aside the impugned order. 

 Accordingly, the appeal is allowed. The impugned order dated 3-2-99 passed by the learned Sessions Judge and Special Tribunal insofar as against the accused appellants namely 1. Shaheb Ali son of Alhaj Md Nabab Ali 2. Abdul Hoque, son of Shiddak Mia and 3. Md Kabir, son Md Abdul Hai is set aside and they are discharged from the proceedings of Special Tribunal Case No.30 of 1998 now pending in the Court of Session Judge and Special Tribunal No. 1 Rangpur.
